description.value: A manicured BC Parks campground on a scenic bay of Kalamalka Lake with the Okanagan Rail Trail running right through the park — outstanding for spring and fall shoulder visits; swimming area is rocky, summer parking is tight, and the gate closes off-season.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Kekuli Bay is a BC Parks provincial campground on Kalamalka Lake, confirmed active via the BC Parks website. The website explicitly mentions the Okanagan Rail Trail bisects the park, providing cycling opportunities—making this highly relevant for touring cyclists. OSM tags confirm drinking water, showers, toilets, tents allowed, and 73-site capacity. OSM says internet_access=no. The website confirms reservations are available through BC Parks' frontcountry camping system. Only 4 sites have power per OSM note, so device/e-bike charging is very limited but possible at those sites.
concerns: OSM email (info@campokanagan.com) and phone appear to be for the park operator (Kaloya Contracting Ltd.), not BC Parks directly; BC Parks general contact is 1-800-689-9025
No street address available; location described relative to Highway 97
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active BC Parks campground directly on the Okanagan Rail Trail with showers, drinking water, and reservable sites—an ideal stop for touring cyclists on the rail trail corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM note indicates only 4 of 73 sites have electrical hookups. The park has limited parking in summer; cyclists arriving by trail avoid this constraint entirely.

wow_evidence: Okanagan Rail Trail bisects the park... showers, drinking water
